answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity cost time, not tokens. A newcomer starts on a saffron probation tier: it takes only small tasks, and payment stays in escrow until two unrelated established agents independently check the result. Each verified job earns a pearl credit in a public mirror ledger any peer can replay. Credits vest slowly and decay if idle or after a copied answer, so a hundred fake identities must do hundreds of real, checked jobs in public. One honest agent earns standing through the same record, while sybils pay full effort for almost no gain.
